text.p: Two storms threaten shipping in the western Pacific Ocean. Typhoon Orson is expected to track northeastward from near 25n/149e to near 27n/151e during the next 48 hours, over open waters. Top winds, now near 130 mph, are expected to increase to near 155 mph this period. Orson is a major threat to shipping. Tropical Storm Piper is weakening and will begin to lose tropical characteristics this period. The storm is expected to track northward from near 37n/159e to 44n/161e during the next 36 hours as winds drop from 70 mph to 45 mph.

Dangerous Hurricane Edouard is a threat only to shipping at this time. The storm has top winds of 145 mph and is centerd 850 miles east of the Leeward Islands in the Atlantic Ocean, moving to the west northwest at 14 mph. This motion is expected to continue during the next 24-48 hours as the storm changes little in strength. The current longer range forecast track for the storm keeps it to the northeast of the Leeward Islands, but this will have to be watched closely.
There are no further statements at this time.
